sections.installation:
1. Install and activate 404Zen through the Plugins screen, or upload the ZIP via Plugins → Add New → Upload.
  2. The first scan starts automatically in the background within a few minutes.
  3. Visit 404Zen in your admin menu to see results, or click Scan now to start immediately.
  4. Adjust scan frequency, batch size, exclusions and the email digest under 404Zen → Settings.
sections.faq:
What makes 404Zen different from other broken link checkers?

Three things: it runs entirely on your own server (your URLs never leave your site), scanning is unlimited and free with no monthly credits, and it doesn’t just report broken links — it grades your whole site A–F and lets you fix links in one click without opening the editor.

Does 404Zen keep monitoring for new broken links?

Yes. Set it to scan hourly, twice daily, daily or weekly and it works as an ongoing 404 monitor — re-checking your site on schedule and updating your Link Health Grade, so new broken links surface on their own instead of waiting for you to look.

Does 404Zen send my data to a third-party service?

No. There is no account to create and no scanning service — all link checking runs on your own server using the WordPress HTTP API, and your URLs never leave your site. Two optional exceptions send data only when you act: the bundled Freemius SDK (Pro licensing/checkout) sends nothing unless you open the upgrade, checkout or license screens, and the product-updates opt-in sends your email only if you explicitly tick it. See the External services section for full details.

Will it slow down my site?

No. Checks run in small background batches via WP-Cron, pause between requests, and stop after a short time budget. 404Zen also watches your server’s load average and skips its run entirely while the server is busy.

What counts as a broken link?

HTTP status 400 and above (404, 410, 500, …), connection failures, DNS errors and timeouts. Links that pass through two or more redirects are flagged separately as redirect chains.

Does it check images?

Yes. Image sources (<img src>) are checked the same way as links. You can turn this off in Settings.

Can I exclude certain URLs or post types?

Yes. Settings lets you exclude any post type and any URL pattern (a simple substring match, one per line).

How do I fix a broken link?

Right from the dashboard: edit the URL inline, unlink it (keeping the text), or dismiss it if it’s a false positive. You never have to open the post editor.

Does it work with WP-Cron disabled?

If you’ve disabled WP-Cron and use a real cron job that calls wp-cron.php, 404Zen works normally. Without any cron at all, scans run opportunistically on page visits, like every other WP-Cron task.

Is 404Zen compatible with multisite?

The free version works on individual sites of a network. Network-wide management is part of 404Zen Pro.

What does my Link Health Grade mean?

A means clean. The grade weighs broken links, redirect chains and how fresh your last scan is. The dashboard explains your current grade and exactly how to raise it.

sections.description:
Broken link checker that finds and fixes 404s, dead links, broken images and redirect chains — fast, private, and light on your server.

The broken link checker that grades your whole site

404Zen is a fast, private broken link checker for WordPress. It scans every post, page, image and menu for broken links, 404 errors, dead links, missing images and redirect chains — entirely on your own server, with no cloud and no account — then distills it all into a single Link Health Grade (A–F) so you know exactly where your site stands.

Broken links quietly cost you visitors and tell Google your content is decaying. 404Zen lets you fix them in one click — edit the URL, unlink it, or dismiss a false positive — without ever leaving WordPress. Your first scan starts automatically the moment you activate. No setup wizard. No limits.

Why site owners choose 404Zen

A grade, not a data dump. One letter tells you instantly whether your links are helping or hurting your SEO, and the dashboard shows exactly what to fix first.

Everything runs on your server. Your URLs never leave your site — no third-party scanning service, no account, private by design.

Unlimited scanning, free forever. No monthly credits, no metering, no “250 links per month” ceiling.

Fixes, not just reports. Edit a URL, unlink it, or dismiss a false positive right from the results table — you never have to open the post editor.

Gentle on your server. Checks run in small background batches with load-aware pausing, tuned for shared hosting rather than just big VPS boxes.

What 404Zen finds

Broken internal and external links (404s), dead links, missing images, redirect chains and loops, timeouts, and DNS failures — all flagged and grouped so you can act on them fast.

Your Link Health Checklist

A guided checklist walks you from your first scan to a clean, protected site — right down to confirming you’re serving HTTPS. Reach 100% and your visitors stop hitting dead ends.

404Zen Pro — set it and forget it

Upgrade when you’re ready for one-click auto-redirects that send visitors from broken URLs straight to the right page, plus CSV exports and multisite management. One license, one flat price, with a lifetime option available — no per-link nickel-and-diming, and a 14-day money-back guarantee.

Built by Zen Plugins — the team behind SSL Zen (★4.9, 1M+ downloads). Focused plugins. Zero bloat.

External services

404Zen checks links on your own server via the WordPress HTTP API. The only outbound requests are: (1) to the URLs in your own content, to test whether they work — no personal data, just the URL being checked and a User-Agent identifying the plugin and your site; (2) to Freemius, only if you open the Pro upgrade, checkout or license screens (bundled SDK, anonymous mode) — see the Freemius Privacy Policy; and (3) to Zen Plugins (https://zenplugins.org/subscribe.php), only if you tick the optional product-updates opt-in, which sends just the email address you enter — see the Zen Plugins privacy policy. Nothing else ever leaves your site.
